main_text.l: rifmo quadragefimoquarto, & quinto,Se-
ctionis quartæ. Quos febres longæ exer-
cent(inquir)ijs tubercula ad articulos, vel
labores fiunt:& mox,quibus tubercula,vel
in articulis labores post febres fiunt, ijs ci-
barijs pluribus utuntur. At huiusmodi fe-
bres absq; aliquo viscere male affecto fieri
non posse, apud omnes medicos est in con-
senso:quod sane ostendit Fernelius libro de
Febribus, ubi intermittentium caufas tra-
dit. Tunc enim ab hepate, & venis in arti-
culos fit fluxio,cum huiusmodi partes tan-
ta grauatur copia,ut eam nec excipere, nec
continere queant: idcirco per emissaria ad
exteriores partes hos supervacaneos hu-
mores propellunt, ubi ob musculorum la-
xitatem nullum excitant dolorem, hinc ve-
rò in articulos, ubi ob adstrictionem par-
tium retinentur. Quoniam autem ibi
sensiles partes, ut ligamenta,
distendunt,idcirco his
partib. dolores
cientur[?].

page.notes: Catchword "EXER-" is at the bottom right. A small mark "R" stands to its left; it is probably a printer's mark and is not transcribed. "hinc ue / rò": the word is split at the line end without a printed hyphen, so it is written whole as "verò". "fesso" in the printed text has been read as "fenso" in "consenso"; the first letters of the word are split across the lines, so the reading is uncertain. Last word "cientur": the reading is doubtful and may be incomplete.
